items.title: Man denies reporting Alan Jones to police in order to 'get money'
items.description: A man accusing Alan Jones of indecently assaulting him as a 17-year-old made a police complaint to "get money", the former broadcaster's lawyer has told a Sydney court.

items.title: Facebook pays controversial creators to produce rage-bait content
items.description: An ABC NEWS Verify investigation reveals Facebook is directly funding some controversial Australian content creators including a white nationalist and an anti-vaxxer influencer.

items.title: 'Colossal stuff-up': AHPRA mass email exposes private doctor information
items.description: The national healthcare watchdog has inadvertently identified more than 100 doctors, nurses and other practitioners who were offered addiction and alcohol misuse training in a mass email that has triggered fierce backlash and privacy complaints.

items.title: Judges dismiss 'excessive' jail sentence complaint from Cassius Turvey's killer
items.description: One of the men convicted of killing Perth teenager Cassius Turvey has failed in his appeal against his nine-year jail sentence, which he claimed was "manifestly excessive".

items.title: Australian silicon company forced out of US by 40pc tariffs
items.description: Australia's only silicon producer will exit the US market next week, but the federal government says the Trump administration's move does not undermine the critical minerals agreement between the two countries.

items.title: Tuvaluans make tough decision to leave for Australia as sea levels rise
items.description: Many Tuvaluans, including Poeva and Akesa's family, are migrating to Australia as sea levels threaten their nation.

items.title: 'Doesn't meet the pub test': ABC apologises to Rinehart over TV show reference
items.description: The ABC apologises for a Race Around the World episode containing remarks about mining magnate Gina Rinehart AO, despite the broadcaster's ombudsman finding it did not breach editorial standards.

items.title: Tax, gambling and migration fights ahead for Labor
items.description: Parliament is yet to resume but the stage has been set for the political fights set to play out next week.

items.title: US military jammed GPS before medical plane crash
items.description: A federal investigation is underway after a medical plane carrying two nurses and two pilots crashed during a military GPS jamming operation in New Mexico.

items.title: Court battle brews over planned crocodile-filled moat at Israeli prison
items.description: A legal battle has erupted in Israel over a government plan to build a moat around a prison and fill it with crocodiles.

items.title: Pauline Hanson does 'not care' if immigration cuts impact businesses
items.description: The One Nation leader says her focus is on a "decent standard of living" and "way of life", saying she does "not care" if cuts to skilled migration will affect businesses.

items.title: Netball's uniform debacle hints at bigger problem for women in sport
items.description: Swifts netballer and professional nutritionist Teigan O'Shannassy says uniform problems are just one of the many difficulties elite female athletes struggling with body image issues face.

items.title: Woman who saved teen from bow and arrow attack given royal bravery award
items.description: A man wielding a bow and arrow attempted to kill a teenage girl at a supermarket. Nicole Law stood in his way.

items.title: Woman facing 62 charges allegedly sent death threats to senior politicians
items.description: A Western Sydney woman allegedly threatened to kill NSW Labor minister Jihad Dib, One Nation leader Pauline Hanson, independent federal MP Allegra Spender and 15 others, NSW Police say.

items.title: Tattoo artists concerned over rise in AI-generated requests
items.description: Tattoo artists are concerned about customers increasingly requesting designs based on AI-generated images, which they say often contain errors and set "unrealistic expectations".

items.title: Year by year, Sydney's winter wonderland is becoming just a memory
items.description: New South Wales is in the middle of its 30th consecutive warmer than average winter — and a past staple of the season is rapidly vanishing.

items.title: Book showcases Australian retro TV from Skippy to Hey Hey It's Saturday
items.description: In a world of rapidly developing technology, television was once considered revolutionary. A new book by Ian Collis, Retro Television: What We Watched Back in the Day, is a nostalgic trip down memory lane.

items.title: Defunct SpaceX rocket crashes into Moon at 8,690km/h
items.description: A stray piece of a rocket, the size of a school bus, has smashed into the Moon, likely creating a new crater.

items.title: 'Manosphere' fuelling extremism in boys and young men, inquiry hears
items.description: Misogyny and its amplification through the "manosphere" may be a key driver of ideologically motivated extremism in young men and boys in Australia, the antisemitism royal commission has heard.

items.title: Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism furore quits, vows 'I will return'
items.description: Professor Jason Arday resigned from his posts shortly after the British institution announced a probe into the various accusations against him.

items.title: Investigations underway into surgery mix-up at Melbourne hospital
items.description: Authorities say they are reviewing how a Melbourne woman was given surgery meant for another patient at a Sunshine hospital.

items.title: Funeral for five-year-old girl Kumanjayi Little Baby confirmed by family
items.description: Months on from the desperate search for five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby by hundreds of volunteers, her grandfather is inviting the community to come together once more for her funeral in Alice Springs later this month.

items.title: Three charged for 'threats' amid probe into Black US teen's shady death
items.description: Three people have been charged for allegedly threatening a US judge, authorities and witnesses connected to the investigation of Black teenager Nolan Wells's mysterious death.

items.title: 'Becomes never-ending': Carnival cruise crew reveal punishing conditions
items.description: Passengers boarding a Carnival cruise ship are promised a world of endless food, relaxation and oceanic luxury. But for the crew who make these escapes possible, life is vastly different.

items.title: New errors uncovered at Queensland's troubled DNA lab
items.description: The latest bungle involved statements the lab provided to police for prosecution, which had typographical errors like the wrong date or case number. The mistake was sensationally first discovered as a scientist was in the witness box giving evidence in June.
